Subject: Re: Quick follow-up from demo (latency/throughput concerns)

Hi Marissa — thanks again for a great demo today. A quick recap from our side and a couple of asks so we can qualify performance/SLOs: 

- Target latency: p95 <= 120ms for short prompts (<= 128 tokens), p95 <= 450ms for long prompts (~1024 tokens)
- Throughput: baseline 300 rps steady-state for our peak market hours (US East)
- Concurrency: expect spikes to 1,200 concurrent requests during market opens
- Streaming: we rely on chunked streaming (SSE) for progressive update UX; tail-latency matters

We want to validate these with a benchmark. Can you share your recommended methodology and a sample prompt set so we can run it against our staging model? Also need to understand measurement definitions (warm vs cold, tokenization, p95 vs p99 sampling) and reproducibility steps.

Thanks,
Alice

Hi Alice — great to hear from you and thanks for the clear targets. Attaching an initial prompt set we use for SLO qualification and a short doc that describes our benchmark harness. High level: 

- We'll capture p50/p95/p99 for per-token and end-to-end request latency, as well as throughput (rps) and successful request ratio.
- We measure both cold-start and warm steady-state. Cold-start = first request to a newly provisioned instance; warm = after a 5 minute priming at target qps.
- For streaming, we report time-to-first-token and time-to-final-token plus tail-latency percentiles.

Attached: edgefin_prompt_set_v1.json, redwood_benchmark_harness.md, latency-throughput-spec.xlsx

Hi Alice — adding some implementation notes so expectations are aligned: 

- Prompt variability: please flag if you have templated prompts vs user-generated content. Our sample set mixes 60% short-form (<=128 tokens), 30% mid (128-512), 10% long (512-1024+). We can adjust to match EdgeFin's real distribution.
- Measurement definitions: 
  * Request latency: measured from request ingress (HTTP accepted) to last-byte-of-response.
  * Token latency: measured at model output tokenization boundaries; useful for streaming comparisons.
  * Throughput: measured as sustained successful requests/sec over 60s windows.
  * Concurrency load: simulated with client concurrency parameter; we recommend ramp-up profiles (linear over 3 mins) to reproduce spikes.
- Environment: we record model version, host GPU type, quantization, batch settings, and seed/LLM deterministic flags for reproducibility.

I'll attach a short YAML config example in the harness doc for your ops team. If you want, Marcus and I can run an initial Redwood-hosted job and share raw metrics/exported CSV.

Neha

Hi Alice — quick answers: 

- Time-to-first-byte p95 <= 60ms for short prompts is feasible on our Dedicated and Hosted fleets with optimized networking and tuned batching (assuming 100% of requests are short-form). If you have mixed-length distribution it adds variance; we recommend separate lanes (short/mid/long) during the benchmark. 
- NVLink isn't strictly required for your numbers; it helps with very large models. We'll start with the GPU types we recommended in the deck (A10G/NVIDIA A30 equivalent) unless you request otherwise.
- Data retention: Redwood can retain raw benchmark logs for 30 days (we'll provide CSV + raw JSON events) and longer retention via our observability add-on.
